question: Your team keeps a project skill in .claude/skills/ that generates test cases for one module, and the CI pipeline runs those tests on each pull request. Developers often invoke the skill without naming a module. In those runs the skill guesses a target, and pull requests arrive with tests for the wrong code. Which change best ensures that developers are asked for the target module when they invoke the skill without arguments?

options.text: Add context: fork to the SKILL.md frontmatter so that the skill runs in an isolated sub-agent context apart from the main conversation.
options.reason: The guide says that context: fork isolates skill output from the main conversation, so it does not ask developers for a missing module parameter.

options.text: Add argument-hint to the SKILL.md frontmatter so that the skill prompts developers for the target module when they give no arguments.
options.reason: The guide says that argument-hint in skill frontmatter prompts developers for required parameters when they invoke the skill without arguments.

options.text: Add a rule file in .claude/rules/ whose YAML frontmatter lists glob patterns for each module so that module conventions load automatically.
options.reason: The guide says that rule files with glob patterns apply conventions based on file paths, so they do not ask developers for a missing module parameter.

options.text: Add allowed-tools to the SKILL.md frontmatter and list only the file read and write tools that the test generation step needs.
options.reason: The guide says that allowed-tools restricts tool access during skill execution, so it does not ask developers for a missing module parameter.
